_why: GREASE, the wizard spell (not the grease flask). The Force-Weaver preset's fourth slot is swapped from Jump to Grease and the book's own flags are swapped with it, because a preset writes its slots directly and then runs prepare_auto_fill, so by the time this script's overrides land the head is already packed with the spell that used to be in that slot -- and prepare_count DROPS anything carried that the book no longer holds, which is correct behaviour and exactly why the pair has to move together here. In play a spell never leaves a book, so this never arises. Then Grease is cast in a real fight. Expect: the Grease option on offer, a wizard slot spent (2 -> 1), and combat_enemy1_greased 3 with combat_enemy1_grease_until six rounds out -- the SAME per-slot fields the grease flask writes, so combat_grease_gate needed no change at all. Rolls are forced high, so the lacedon makes its best Dexterity save: whether it goes prone is up to the roll, the slick is not.

stats.wizard_spell_4_desc: Grease—a slick of caustic grease conjured across the ground under a foe and everything standing with it.
